result.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length
result.comment: 36 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables; supplementary material included as an ancillary file. Submitted to SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences. Code: https://github.com/michael-werman/realizability-code
result.summary: When is an image ellipse the outline of a given ellipsoid with semi-axes $a <= b <= c? For a camera with square pixels, zero skew and known principal point, we show that it is an outline at focal length $f$ exactly when a cone ratio kappa(f), computed from two eigenvalues, is at most a/c; the middle semi-axis b plays no role. With f unknown, the admissible focal lengths form an interval; whether it is empty is decided by the smallest cone ratio over $f$, which, when attained, is obtained from an explicit quartic. The interval is bounded above only when the principal point is closer to the long axis of the ellipse than to its short axis. Thus one ellipse can rule out ellipsoids that are too round, never ones that are too elongated, and none if the principal point is unknown. Simulations and 45 Cassini images of Saturn's moons support the test.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究给定椭球的图像椭圆能否成为其轮廓：在方像素、零倾斜、主点已知的相机模型下，提出由两个特征值构成的锥比 κ(f)，并证明 κ(f)≤a/c 即为可行条件；焦距未知时可行区间由最小锥比与显式四次方程决定，并以仿真和土星卫星图像验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 该判定给出「单个图像椭圆作为几何证据可排除过圆椭球、却无法排除过扁椭球」的明确可行性与不可判定边界，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、几何假设一致性检验及证据不足时的停止判断提供可核查的形式化参照，但与 latent 状态生成无直接关系。
